conclusion: The premise that combining established repositories should automatically yield a well-trained MARVEL+GPPO policy is not supported. The implemented network/optimizer primitives can be reused, but this experiment changes the learning environment, reward, state, action authority, communication criterion and training scale. It is a new hierarchical physical-loop adaptation, not a verified reproduction of the paper's GPPO task. This establishes a task/protocol mismatch; it does not by itself prove an implementation error in the current PPO sampling or gradients.

decision_on_user_premise.supported: It is reasonable to demand reuse of existing architectures,optimizer primitives and simulator components instead of inventing additional mechanisms. Current evidence also supports auditing task/reward/action/sampling contracts before further expensive collection.
decision_on_user_premise.unsupported: There is no verified pair of ready-made official MARVEL+GPPO repositories implementing the same state/action/reward environment and jointly trained checkpoint. Therefore plug them together and it should learn well is not an established engineering premise.
decision_on_user_premise.not_a_proven_cause: Task mismatch and small new sample count are strong reasons performance transfer is unproven. They do not identify the sole cause of heldout regression or prove that simply matching paper hyperparameters fixes it.
decision_on_user_premise.no_new_mechanism_recommendation: Do not respond to this finding with anotherplanner,featureexpansion,probe mechanism or heldout-driven model reselection. First distinguish paper reproduction from physical-task adaptation and audit whether current high-level actions carry sufficient controllable signal for the chosen target.
